The house brain: "turn the music down a notch" is a plain route, and a quip's "try not to" no longer makes a claim look honest in the music re-ask

Two small things the last trials on the real Core showed, after the fifth review's fixes (29e89a3).

music_route strips a degree word after a volume command like it strips "a bit" and "a little": a notch, a touch, a tad, one notch, slightly. "turn the music down a notch", the phrase these trials used, went to the model, and in 2 of 24 trials the model claimed it in words only; the re-ask then answered with a text call the house cannot read about half the time (6 of 12 forced re-asks done; a stronger nudge made no difference, and Core ignores tool_choice). Now it is the plain quieter or louder.

_honest took the "not" of a quip's "try not to" for a retraction, so a second try that claimed again ("Quieter now. Try not to strain your tiny ears.") was spoken with nothing done. QUIP_NEGATIONS is taken out first, as everywhere else the claim path looks for a retraction.

The _tool_brackets docstring now says the plain-words clause (a bracket holding one of the tool's own action words is a call) and what it costs. The README records both changes and what is still open: a question mark still makes a second try honest even when it claims after the question.

30 new tests (15 of them fail without the two changes). Satellite suite and the property runs re-run on this tree.

A fresh reviewer attacked the merge of the fourth review's patches and found five things, each reproduced here before it was fixed.

A (high): the words after the reasoning took its call back when they held a question mark or a retraction word anywhere, so "There. Quieter. Happy now?" or "Sorry, my magnificence was too loud. Quieter now." dropped the call and the false claim was spoken (12 of 13 such replies). They now take it back only when every sentence is a question or a retraction (_takes_back); "can't believe" and "couldn't resist" are no retraction.
D (medium): announces() let any sentence with a question mark through, so "Done, happy now?" or "I've cancelled it, okay?" passed a second try that had done nothing (6 of 6). A question that opens with the claim or the promise still claims (_CLAIM_OPENS); honest questions stay honest.

B (low-medium): _NOT_MEANT missed the typographic apostrophe and "cannot" ("I shouldn’t call [music action=next]" skipped a track).
E (low): the line before a call was read whole, quadratic on a line of thousands of calls; it is now at most 120 characters.

A hub restart after the evening check time (21:30) ran the check at once, a second before the router had opened the Enclave, so at 22:30 on
2026-11-05 his phone was told "the upstairs speaker isn't connected" when it was. AlarmClock now judges only SETTLE_S (120 s) after it was made;
the day is not marked checked until then, and a speaker that really is off is still reported once. Two tests (one fails on the old behaviour).

tools/tts_bench.py had been broken since the voice gate dropped gate.LOCAL_VOICES (and changed Voice's arguments): fixed, and "--whole" asks for
one run per reply as the house hub does. Measured live on the rebuilt stack, Skippy's voice, single-sentence lines: first audio 1.29 s per
sentence mode, 0.71 s whole-reply mode.

The direct door's pages, proved in a real browser: a door cut under a song, a book or a film now goes on from the Funnel in about twenty seconds, and a book whose place save already moved its pass is no longer left silent

Found by driving the real Drive, Bilby, Audiobooks, Nagatha and chat-upload pages (Chrome 152) against a loopback door and Funnel whose logs say which one every request reached; each fix was proved before and after in the same harness.
- Drive/HUD: resumeOnFunnel asked where the PASS pointed, not where the audio element's own request went, so after a failed place save had moved the book's pass to the Funnel the book never resumed (0 Funnel requests); it now asks the element's address. A door that takes a request and never answers, or goes quiet mid-stream, raises no audio error at all (182 s with nothing): a 20 s stall watcher on `waiting` sends the same song or book on from the Funnel, at the same position.
- Audiobooks: the same watcher (a cut door raised its error only 92 s later, a quiet one never).
- Nagatha: Chrome fires one more `timeupdate` about 250 ms after `waiting`, which defeated the film's stall rule (74 s); a `stalled` listener, as Bilby's player has, restores it (19 s).
Also passing in the real browser: the door picked and used when healthy, the Funnel when it is down at load, a catalog fetch that fails after the probe, Bilby's signal-lost loop re-asking the portal and coming back on the Funnel at the same position, Retry re-probing, the chat upload retried once on the Funnel, a pass with no door sending nothing to it, and no uncaught exception anywhere.
